messages:
maria: Quick note  after the priority-aging deploy (~18:12 UTC) the /generate-route p95 jumped ~115ms in the rollout dashboard. p50 stable. Canary alarm tripped. Anyone else?

alex: Saw it live. Traces indicate low-priority requests are experiencing more queue_wait. My initial theory: preemption windows are fragmenting batches for low-pri which increases per-request overhead.

jin: Ran a focused rollup query (split by phase + priority):
```
SELECT priority_level, phase, percentile(latency_ms,50) p50, percentile(latency_ms,95) p95, count(*) samples
FROM telemetry.traces
WHERE endpoint = '/generate-route' AND ts >= now() - interval '6 hours'
GROUP BY priority_level, phase
```
Results: high-pri queue p95 ~82ms (samples 122k), low-pri queue p95 ~380ms (samples 4.2k). Compute-phase p95s are similar (~60-85ms). So queue_wait looks like the culprit.

sam: Notably overall p99 barely moved, so this is a mid-tail cohort effect (p95) not an extreme tail regression. Could be the variant-b fallback or retries triggering for low-pri under load.

lia: We do have a fallback that routes to variant-b when queue_depth > 1.1k; variant-b adds ~90-110ms for some payload shapes. Audit logs show increased variant-b decisions in the same window.

telemetry-bot: telemetry-bot: snapshot uploaded -> https://redwood.internal/telemetry/snapshots/6171717000 (includes rollup CSV and trace ids)

alex: Two immediate product/console actions: (1) surface phase-separated percentiles (queue_wait vs service_time) for endpoints in the latency pane so percentiles aren't hiding phase regressions; (2) show sample_count next to each percentile and add a low-sample confidence badge. Right now a single merged latency percentile can be misleading when phase mix changes.

maria: Agreed. Also annotate the dashboard with the priority-aging deploy (PR #3456) timestamp so metric deltas can be correlated to config/deploy events.

jin: I'll prototype rollup dimensions adding `phase` and `priority_level` and compute per-minute percentiles. Example:
```
SELECT phase, priority_level, percentile(latency_ms,95) p95, count(*) samples
FROM telemetry_rollups
WHERE endpoint='/generate-route' AND window='1m'
GROUP BY phase, priority_level
```
Prelim output: p95(queue|low)=335ms, p95(compute|low)=64ms  confirms queue dominates.

sam: Also verify sampling policy for canaries. Some canaries use higher-fidelity sampling which can overweight slower debug clients. Add a sampling-sanity gate: flag percentile buckets with samples < 500 as low-confidence.

lia: UX suggestion: in endpoint breakdown hover tooltip show p50/p95/p99 split by phase as tiny stacked bars (queue vs compute). Quick triage.

maria: I'll file a small UX ticket to add: (A) per-phase p50/p95/p99 in latency pane, (B) sample_count + confidence badge in the legend/tooltips, (C) auto-annotation for config/deploy events with PR link. Who wants the rollup/query work?

alex: I can own the dashboard wiring and deploy annotation metadata.

jin: I'll update rollup ingestion to emit `priority_level` and `phase` dims and implement the low-sample alert. I'll also export trace_ids for the slow low-pri cohort for postmortem if needed.

telemetry-bot: telemetry-bot: created INF-12021 "Latency: phase split + sample_count + deploy annotations" and attached a mock image.

sam: One more product note: default the latency pane to phase-separated view for endpoints that experience queueing; make the combined "total latency" an opt-in aggregate. That should reduce churn where p95 shifts due to queue mix changes.

maria: Love that. After the PRs land we'll re-run canary gating and check p95. If queue_wait for low-pri remains high we can tune aging windows or bump fallback hysteresis. Thanks all for quick triage.
